newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines blame gov't policies for jobless - poll.
newsitem.headline: Argentines blame gov't policies for jobless - poll.

text.p: A majority of Argentines blame the economic policies of President Carlos Menem for the country's 17.3 percent unemployment rate, according to a poll by Graciela Romer y Asociados.

The poll of 800 people in the capital found 58 percent think the high unemployment rate is a result of the government's economic policies and 22 percent said it was a product of global economic conditions. The poll was published by the daily Pagina 12.
Only 14 percent agreed with the government's view that the jobless rate is a consequence of excessive rigidities in the labor market which discourage firms from hiring more workers.
The government has launched an ambitious plan to reform the labor market by breaking down centralized union bargaining.

At the same time, the poll found 39 percent of respondents want the current economic policies to continue, albeit with modifications, 38 percent want a total change in policies while 11 percent are happy with the status quo.
The paper did not specify the poll's margin of error.
